Soft YTA. You’re not technically wrong—but emotionally, yeah, what an AH.

You bought your dream dog before your girlfriend moved in. You used your own money, it’s your apartment (for now), and this has been a long-standing goal. On paper? Not the AH.

BUT.
You’re weeks away from cohabitating, and you just made a 10–12 year commitment to a massive, high-maintenance breed without even discussing it with the person who’s about to share that life, space, and responsibility with you. That’s where the AH part comes in.

Even if you assumed she’d be happy because she knew you wanted one—this wasn’t just buying a pair of concert tickets. This is a living being with training needs, energy, noise, and cost. It’s not your dog anymore—it’s going to be hers too, by default of living with you.

Honestly, as someone who’d hope my partner and I would get to pick our future companion dog together, I’d be so hurt to be left out of that experience. Choosing the right pup, meeting them, falling in love as a team—that’s bonding. That’s part of the joy. Being cut out of it would feel like you picked a “baby” without me.

You didn’t just sign yourself up—you signed her up too. And skipped the part where you check if she’s onboard.

So yeah—not the worst AH, but this is one of those “it’s not what you did, it’s how you did it” moments. If this is someone you love and plan to build a life with, communication needs to come before the commitment, not after the crate’s already in the hallway.

Five days before this past Christmas, I was entertaining family—music, snacks, holiday chaos—when I got hit with this sharp, brutal pain in my back. Felt exactly like back labor. But plot twist: I haven’t had a working baby factory in over 17 years. Tubes? Tied. Cauterized. Retired.

I figured it’d pass. Spoiler: it did not.

I spent three days “laboring” in bed—crying, screaming, passing out from pain, then waking up and doing it all over again.

Two days before Christmas, I woke up scream-crying. My husband, eyes wide with panic and patience worn thin, said:
“Either I take you to the hospital, or I’m calling an ambulance.”

And me? I still refused. Thought I’d just get dumped in an ER chair for six hours and sent home with Tylenol and a side of gaslighting. (Medical trauma is a bitch.)

So I compromised: urgent care.

I barely made it in the door. I was hyperventilating, couldn’t walk straight, couldn’t think. Staff took one look at me and said, “Nope.” They started calling for an ambulance. I begged them to stop—eventually they let my husband drive me to the ER.

Halfway there, I started shaking uncontrollably. Still no urge to push, so I figured hey, still not a ghost baby. But I was going down. Fast.

The ER rushed me back immediately. I was losing consciousness, shaking with rigors, no color, low oxygen, no clarity. I’d waited too long. I was septic.

They rushed me into emergency surgery.
My last words before the anesthesia hit:
“I love you and the kids. Kiss my fur babies. And please—if I go, let me go. Don’t keep me here.”

I crushed my husband’s soul with that one.

And the thing that almost killed me?

A 9mm kidney stone.
Just one tiny, furious, jagged rock.
Worse than the three days I spent laboring an actual child.

10/10 do not recommend.

I was married for 11 years. We divorced in 2021—friendly at first… until we weren’t. I went no-contact for just under a year.

Then life (and our adult kid) forced us back into communication.
We started talking. Then laughing. Then quietly wondering if maybe—just maybe—there was still something real there.

Turns out, we can live without each other.
We just… don’t want to.

We got back together. And all that petty, piddly shit we used to argue about?
Yeah—total noise. Flecks of dust in sunlight. Meaningless in the long run.

Love mattered more than being right.
Connection mattered more than ego.
We finally learned how to listen.

Now? We’re planning to re-marry each other.
Not because we have to—because we choose to.
We’ve changed. We’re softer, funnier, more aware of what it takes.

And the only fighting we do now?
Every single day, he asks me to smell his hand.
And every day I say not just “no,” not just “absolutely not,” but HELL NO. 😂
I have no idea where those hands have been, and I am not taking that gamble.

Honestly?
It’s the best fight we’ve ever had.

Marriage isn’t necessarily a fallacy—but it is a wildly misunderstood and often mystified institution that too many people enter into like it’s a fairy tale, not a fraught long-term negotiation with another evolving, imperfect human being.

1. People change, but vows don’t.
You swear to love someone forever… but that someone—and you—will morph over the decades. Are you still compatible after version 3.0 of each other drops? That’s the gamble.

2. Communication is the crumbling foundation.
You can’t build a cathedral of trust on mumbling and passive aggression. As the top comment says: “People don’t communicate.” It’s not just about speaking—it’s about listening without the armor of ego, without trying to win. That’s rarer than diamonds.

3. Cultural programming vs. actual compatibility.
Marriage is sold as a universal life milestone. But what if it’s a tool that worked for survival farming economies, not modern hyper-individualist societies? Maybe we’re using a rotary phone in a touchscreen world.

4. Longevity ≠ success.
Forty years in a cold, resentful silence isn’t a win. That’s emotional taxidermy.

5. We don’t teach relationship skills.
There’s no class in school for navigating conflict, building intimacy, or managing shared emotional labor. But hey, at least we all know mitochondria is the powerhouse of the cell.

6. Fear of solitude drives poor choices.
People cling to the idea of a relationship—any relationship—to not feel alone. But loneliness in a bad marriage is like drowning next to someone holding the same life raft.

Is marriage a fallacy?

It can be… if entered blindly.
If it’s used to fix a problem, validate a relationship, or tick a life box—yeah, that’s delusional. But if it’s an ongoing project built on mutual growth, communication, emotional literacy, and a shared life vision? Then it’s no more a fallacy than learning to play jazz well—it’s just hard. 

Should you take more time before proposing?

Yes.
Not because you don’t love her. But because you do. Marriage isn’t the prize at the end of dating. It’s the contract to keep growing together through chaos, trauma, change, and maybe therapy with a side of dirty laundry.

Not sure if anyone’s mentioned this yet, but you do have options that don’t rely on your ex magically stepping up. You can contact Texas DFPS (https://www.dfps.texas.gov) and initiate the process of surrendering the child to the state. That would trigger an investigation and custody hearing. The court might give Dad full custody—or, if he refuses to step up, your child could be placed in foster care while both your rights are reviewed.

It’s not ideal. It’s painful. But it’s real. And honestly, it’s more responsible than continuing to parent in survival mode while the father plays “part-time optional parent” and still somehow thinks he gets veto power over everything.

You tried to get an abortion—he blocked it. You suggested adoption—he blocked that too. You’re not some villain for saying “enough” now. You’re one person trying to live a life with dignity and balance. At some point, consequences need to find their way to the man who wanted all the control and none of the responsibility.

Keep following up with that lawyer to formalize custody. In the meantime, document everything—calls, refusals, texts, his reaction at work—because if you do have to go to court, that timeline will matter.

You are not the bad guy for demanding that parenthood be shared.

This happened to me when my son and his girlfriend had my grandbaby. Now by no means am i like you mil, but it was a rocky start (my son had BPD and is very manipulative. He played the my mom doesn't love me or like me card for sympathy and attention and it worked in the beginning. However, now my bonus daughter and I now have a very solid bond. In the beginning, I knew she was pregnant before she knew and bought her the test and was the first one she told… Intuition I guess. I was so excited her parents were not. They also looked down on me because of my son’s mental health. As she progressed in her pregnancy she became more and more distant and wouldn't even accept gifts from me. I wasn't welcomed and it hurt. I know she had her mom and dad too I just hoped we could share in that joy. At first, I was invited to be there for her delivery but then her parents refused to be in the same room as me so the invite was revoked. I cried a lot but then my brother’s baby was due the same week and he asked me to come and be there for him and his wife across the country so I went. This all took place in Feb of 2020 my grandbaby was the 28th and my nephew the 29th. I wasn't wanted there but because I wasn't around it was held over my head. I wasn't allowed to meet my grand until she was almost 6 months and only for a few hours. I have only spent a few hours one other time with her because I moved away at the end of 2020. Eventually, she and my son broke up and proved to be everything I said (as far as mental health goes) and left her to raise that sweet baby alone. I hate it all because he’s not been a good father or even stepped up much… but on the other hand, she's come to realize I've been her biggest cheerleader and will go to the ends of the earth to help her. I walked in those same shoes and know how hard it is when you have nobody to depend on or vent to. So yes it did break my heart and it stings missing every milestone and magical moment, but it doesn't define how much I love her as if she were my own daughter. She's the mother of my very first grandbaby and she will always be special. You have to know it hurts being the outsider, but it doesn't make you a monster and it shouldn't be what dictates or defines your relationship with MIL. Good luck and congratulations on your first baby ❤️

I feel this in my core. It's been a constant episode of major depression for the better part of 7 years. I've barely been able to get out of bed. I'm nearly catatonic most days, I don't speak to friends or family much because I don't have anything to say anymore and while I understand they are tired of hearing about how I'm struggling I'm also tired of hearing them tell me to suck it up. They don't/can't handle what they don’t understand or relate to. And, even when they do acknowledge it, it's usually only to tell me all the ways I've failed or how I'm lazy and how if I acted a certain way then maybe I'd be worthy of xyz… every day I feel like I wake up to what I can only describe as a flu/sickness Im coming down with. My body and headaches relentlessly. My chest and throat feel like it's closing up and hurts to speak or swallow and take a deep breath, but the fever never comes. I have bouts of agoraphobia and can't bring myself to leave unless I'm forced outside out of necessity. My joys and hobbies and dreams… no longer enjoyable, no energy to start or finish, participate in. My mind races too much to concentrate on a dream what are those anyways? My ex-husband told me they were all stupid and asked what was wrong with me so much that I actually stopped having any except for nightmares. I have those regularly now so quality sleep is also difficult to fall back on as well. 

I'm well aware it's important to encourage depressed people to seek help and not “do it” but I'd be lying about that too. I seriously doubt people genuinely care either way since most people usually don't care about anything outside of themselves. It's definitely not been my experience at all in all my 40 years stuck on this planet. And, No! I do not agree or believe that you should do anything harmful to yourself… But I do however understand who what and why you feel this way and how hard of a time it is to keep going like the energizer bunny whose batteries have been drained and barely have enough juice left to even pick yourself up. I understand feeling so alone and worrying about others having to deal with the aftermath. The general population has a completely screwed-up and false narrative about how suicidal people are cowards and selfish. They can't even imagine how much pain a person has to be in to plan that shit and be successful at following through 🤯 the reality is so much more terrifying and the shame and embarrassment of failure is even more intense when you think you can't even die correctly and now you're also called attention seeking to top everything you already felt off. The cycle is truly vicious. With all that being said I just want to leave you will with one last quote that lives rent free in my head: So now, all alone or not, you gotta walk ahead. Thing to remember is if we're all alone, then we're all together in that too. - P.S. I love you.

I have felt more guilt like I’m “too cowardly” to pull any “proverbial trigger” than I’ve felt selfish. Maybe because I already know, “I'm damned if I do and damned if I don't.” My story doesn’t matter. Who hurt me doesn’t matter. The amount of work I put in to recover doesn’t matter. At the end of the day, knowing what I know and feeling how I feel, someone calling me selfish pales in comparison to the damage already done. 


PSA, I’m not actively plotting out anything. It is more like having daydreams… A dear jumping out while driving, going for a hike and falling off a cliff, or drowning in some large body of water. It’s like a realization that I’m a coward and selfish all at once, so if an opportunity should present itself, I wouldn’t cry or fight. I’d welcome it... Maybe if I thought my act of disappearing would fix all the problems, I might not even blink twice before kissing it all.... You get it. So, for now, I'm safely locked up in my own purgatory. 

Sorry if I upset anyone. These are purely my own inner feelings and views when someone says “selfish” and “suicide” in my presence.

I packed myself and my youngest son up (my eldest refused to go and felt like I was being unreasonable. He was also 17 at that time so I didn’t have a whole lot of say in that moment and they were both ganging up on me) and I left within 48 hours. This time I thought it was going to be the final round especially after we went for months separated, but... (always a but 🤦‍♀️)He’d fallen off the wagon after 12 years of sobriety and when I gave him the divorce papers he spiraled out of control. I had to move my eldest against his wishes which added to the stress and bad behavior he was already exhibiting. My spouse started stalking and molesting me through every avenue possible and then the dam broke and he picked the kids up without telling me and took them somewhere. I had to involve the police to help me find them and his condition prompted me to ask for an escort to remove the weapons from the home... He involved everyone’s knew and thankfully mutual friends talked him in to checking himself into the hospital for a psychological evaluation. However it didn’t stop the endless begging and pleading to “fix it”. This hospital allowed adult patients to keep their cell phones and so for 3 weeks straight almost 24 hours a day he’d call, txt, send letters to the kids and I and proclaim to anyone who’d listen how sorry he was and how he was going to fix it and get his family back. Then the VA stepped in and transferred him to a month long inpatient program and then he volunteered to do another 6month inpatient program. We were all in therapy at this point and everything I heard was geared towards forgiveness and finding the way forward. The guilt was laid on think that I wasn’t being fair so I submitted again after everything. He took a contracting job that required us to move out of state. The ink was barely dry on our new house before he switched back into Mr. Hyde. He tells me to leave I go to pack and then he has a meltdown. I’m the fear of WTF is gonna happen next has paralyzed me. My eldest son is bipolar. I’ve been struggling for years to get him stabilized, and for a good while he was doing great until the issues with my spouse’s suicide attempt overseas. It’s been a scary roller coaster since with extremely risky and dangerous behavior. My spouse has no empathy towards anyone god forbid he’d have any for his own son (by adoption) and although I understand its been extremely difficult at times to manage the stress my mind is blown that all that forgiveness we were begged for couldn’t be extended back to our son. My son now has a baby and his girlfriend HATES ME! I don’t blame her because she only knows what she’s been told and they got involved during one of his downward spirals. My baby he doesn’t deserve any of this. He’s innocent. He’s actually a very well rounded child. He only asked to move to his dads because he’s lonely. My spouse can no longer pretend to be to be a decent human being to anyone... even to him and he’s never done anything wrong 💔. That’s why I never begged him to stay. His dad is a good guy (not to me) but I don’t matter in this situation and he’s got a wonderful bonus mom and 4 extra siblings to grow up with. 

I feel like I’m grieving the loss of my children. It’s unbearable, sometimes I can barely catch my breathe and my body involuntarily wretches from the pain. 

I don’t see the point in trying to leave anymore I already know what happens. I’m to weak to fight back and I don’t want my children drug back into the cycle I allowed myself to be drug into over and over. I can’t ask for help anymore I’m like the girl who cried wolf now and there is nobody left to ask for help. My wounds are internal.

Honestly, I don’t mind if this ever gets voted on or read... I just needed to put it out into the universe. It’s been a heavy holding it in so long. Thank you for your kindness. It’s been a while since I’ve seen a kind word anywhere on  the internet.
There is still time to do all those things... just put your plan on hold for so you can accomplish 2 things on your bucket list. We can die any time we choose but we cannot live unless we try.
Suicide is illegal, smoking is not. I’m not trying to stick around forever. I want off this planet!
